Commentary.Commentary: ADIOS - That's a wrap from the commentary box. The rain has won today, and it has been a frustrating day for both the players and the fans, who waited all day only to be denied any cricket. But let's turn our attention toward the third and final match of this series, which will be played on 2nd May. Don't forget to tune in early for all the pre-match build-up. Until then, stay safe and goodbye!

Washout in Chattogram - Bad news folks, the second T20 of this three-match series between Bangladesh and New Zealand has been ABANDONED DUE TO RAIN. The rain was persistent throughout the day, and both captains have now shaken hands to officially call it off. Bangladesh thus retain their lead in the series at 1-0, and the third and final match will be a must-win for New Zealand. The Kiwis can only level the series in Mirpur on 2nd May, however, the trophy is already out of their reach.
Update 9.55 am GMT - Not a single soul on the ground at the moment. It continues to rain, and as things stand, we are running out of time and overs. The chances of any action look very grim.
The cut-off time to start a 5-over game is 10.50 am GMT.

The IPL drama - Rajasthan Royals successfully chased down a massive target to give the Punjab Kings their first loss of the season. Punjab batted first and posted a huge score of 222/4, powered by Marcus Stoinis' smashing 62 runs towards the end. In response, Rajasthan reached 228/4 in 19.2 overs to win the game. Fifteen-year-old star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi gave Rajasthan a flying start with 43. Yashasvi Jaiswal also chipped in with 51 runs, while Donovan Ferreira sealed the win with an unbeaten 52 runs. The action doesn’t stop here. Buckle up for the next massive clash as MI goes against SRH at 2 pm GMT. You won't want to miss it!
Update 9 am GMT - Nothing new to update. The rain is still delaying the game. The covers stay on, and the ground staff is making sure that the outfield is safe. Ugh, this is frustrating.

About the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup - Since the rain is currently keeping the players off the field, it’s the perfect time to look ahead at what’s brewing for the 2026 ICC Women's T20 World Cup. Coming off the back of India’s historic 50-over title win last year, the spotlight returns to the shortest format as England and Wales prepare to host the tournament. But this World Cup is a bit special. Why? This edition is set to be a landmark moment for women's cricket, featuring an expanded roster of 12 teams for the first time. The journey will culminate at the Home of Cricket, with the final scheduled to take place at the iconic Lord’s, promising a massive stage for the next world champions. The group stages are already shaping up, and the fixtures are out as well. Group 1 is headlined by a fierce rivalry between India and the dominant Australians, alongside South Africa, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the Netherlands. Meanwhile, Group 2 features the hosts, England, who will be desperate to reclaim global silverware on home turf. They face a tough road against the defending T20 champions, New Zealand, as well as the West Indies, Sri Lanka, Scotland, and Ireland. The inclusion of more teams means a more grueling path to the knockouts, leaving very little room for error from the opening match at Edgbaston, Birmingham, where the hosts will face Sri Lanka on the 12th of June.

A quick chat with Katene Clarke - Katene Clarke says that he focuses on getting runs on the board, and they can score runs as they have a good team. Adds that he doesn't have WhatsApp, so he couldn't get in touch with his family directly, but messages were passed to his dad when he got his fifty. He says that he needs to bat with more focus, and hopefully, they can win this game.

Eyes on the skies - While the cricketing action promises to be intense, Mother Nature might have the final say today. With heavy rain soaking the ground on Tuesday and showers threatening to interrupt play today, fans and players alike will be crossing their fingers that the weather holds up long enough for a complete and thrilling contest. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Kiwis seeking redemption - Under pressure to respond, New Zealand will be desperate to tighten their bowling attack and find crucial breakthroughs in the middle overs. The potential return of regular skipper Tom Latham from injury, if he manages to recover, could provide the exact spark the visitors need to level the playing field.

Tigers on the prowl - Bangladesh enters tonight’s clash brimming with confidence following their brilliant chase of 183 in the first match. Thanks to Towhid Hridoy's unbeaten heroics, explosive death-over batting, and disciplined spin bowling from Rishad Hossain and Mahedi Hasan, the Tigers are looking to maintain their aggressive edge and seal the series.

Welcome to the showdown - Welcome to Chattogram for the highly anticipated second T20I between Bangladesh and New Zealand. With the hosts riding high on a thrilling, series-opening victory, the stage is set for an electric encounter as the Blackcaps will look to fight and bounce back to keep the series alive.

The Tigers eye a historic series clinch - The narrative of this three-match T20I series has tilted dramatically in favour of the hosts following a masterclass in aggressive batting during the opening encounter. Bangladesh currently sits in the driver's seat with a 1-0 lead after pulling off a sensational six-wicket victory. By successfully hunting down a daunting target of 183, their highest-ever T20I chase on home soil, the Tigers have shed their reputation for being conservative in high-scoring affairs. As the teams remain in the coastal city of Chattogram for this pivotal second clash, the stakes couldn't be higher. For Bangladesh, it is a golden opportunity to secure an unassailable lead and claim a rare series win against a major cricketing powerhouse. For the visitors, it is a fight for survival. Maintaining momentum through discipline - For the hosts to replicate their success and wrap up the series, they must lean heavily on the rock-solid stability of their middle order while seeking more intent from their openers. The spotlight remains firmly on Tawhid Hridoy, whose breathtaking, unbeaten 51 off just 27 deliveries proved he is the engine room of this batting unit. However, the coaching staff will be urging Tanzid Hasan and Litton Das to provide a more explosive launchpad in the Powerplay to take the pressure off the finishers. On the bowling front, the Tigers showed remarkable composure at the death in the first game. The tactical battle will likely be won or lost in the middle overs, where the guile of Rishad Hossain’s leg-spin and the clever variations of Shoriful Islam and Ripon Mondol must be utilised to stifle the Kiwi scoring rate and prevent a good outing with the bat for the visitors. Young blood under the pump - Faced with a must-win scenario and missing a core group of veteran stars due to ongoing franchise commitments, the Black Caps are looking toward their next generation to anchor the comeback. There were flashes of brilliance in the series opener, most notably the fluent half-centuries from Katene Clarke and Dane Cleaver, yet the team was haunted by a mid-innings stagnation that saw them fall short of the 200-run mark, a threshold often deemed necessary on this flat Chattogram surface. NZ faces a significant leadership challenge, with Latham missing the first game and his availability for the second game unclear as well. Nick Kelly, stand-in skipper, must find a way to inspire a more clinical performance from his bowling attack, which struggled to maintain discipline once the field spread. The visitors need to strike a balance between aggression and strike rotation to ensure that a promising start doesn't fizzle out during the crucial 7-15-over window. Form guide (last five T20Is, most recent first) - BAN - WWWLL   | NZ - LWWLL. Series stakes and survival - Historically, New Zealand has been the dominant force in this rivalry, boasting 15 wins to Bangladesh's 5, but those statistics feel increasingly distant given the Tigers' recent evolution in the shortest format. For the Black Caps, this is a test of their depth and adaptability, and they must tighten their lines, refine their spin-bowling variations, and play with the desperation of a team with their backs against the wall. Conversely, Bangladesh is playing with a newfound swagger, fueled by local support and a deep understanding of the conditions. Should the visitors fail to level the series, they risk a sweep in a region where the hosts are becoming increasingly difficult to beat.
